findings.evidence: "Station staff can also help with the same request in person." appears verbatim after both "review the updated schedule" and "report a service issue"
findings.fix: Write a distinct, task-specific sentence for each paragraph (or remove the boilerplate line if it adds no real information).
findings.location: Section s1, paragraphs s1-p1 and s1-p2
findings.violation: The same boilerplate sentence is reused for two unrelated requests, making it read as templated filler rather than specific guidance tied to either task.

findings.evidence: alt="Crews repainting the accessible parking spaces near the station entrance." on src="/img/platform-update.jpg" inside a section titled "Station updates" about reviewing schedules
findings.fix: Verify the image matches the section's topic and rewrite the alt text to accurately describe the actual image content in context.
findings.violation: The alt text describes parking-lot repainting while the filename and surrounding content are about schedule/platform updates, suggesting the wrong image or wrong alt text was used.

findings.evidence: "Riders can report a service issue by calling rider services." duplicates s1-p2's "Commuters can report a service issue by calling rider services."
findings.fix: State the "report an issue by phone" instruction once, and cross-link to it from the other section instead of repeating it.
findings.violation: The same instruction is repeated almost verbatim in two different sections with only the subject noun swapped, creating redundant, bloated content.

findings.evidence: "Local residents can check real time arrivals through the online portal." duplicates s2-p1's "Passengers can check real time arrivals through the online portal."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence from the fare-adjustments section or replace it with fare-specific content; keep the real-time arrivals instruction only in the schedule section.
findings.violation: This is the same real-time-arrivals instruction restated with a different subject noun, adding redundant content under the "Fare adjustments" heading where it is off-topic.

findings.evidence: "Route adjustments take effect on the posted effective date."
findings.fix: Replace with a concrete date or a direct link/reference to where the effective date is published.
findings.violation: This sentence is circular/uninformative - it says adjustments take effect on "the posted effective date" without stating what that date is or where it is posted.

findings.evidence: "Riders can check real time arrivals at any station kiosk. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Delete this duplicated card content or consolidate all "where to check status" guidance into a single statement used once per page.
findings.violation: Both sentences duplicate content already stated elsewhere (real-time arrivals in s2-p1/s3-p2, "updates post within one business day" in s3-p1), compounding redundancy within the same section.

findings.evidence: `<div class="icon-delete" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" id="s3-customcontrol">` with a trash icon, inside a "Fare adjustments" section
findings.fix: Remove this control if it's unrelated leftover markup, or if needed, replace it with a native `<button>` element and ensure it has an associated, meaningful action.
findings.violation: A "Delete item" control is unrelated to fare adjustments content and has no apparent purpose on this page; additionally it's a non-native button (div with role="button"/tabindex) with no visible keyboard event handling, which typically requires manual Enter/Space key handling that native buttons provide for free.

findings.evidence: "Choose a plan" / "Enter payment details" / "Confirm your order" steps under the "Fare adjustments" heading
findings.fix: Remove this unrelated wizard block, or if a real purchase flow belongs here, rewrite the steps to match actual fare-adjustment content and mark them up as an `<ol>`.
findings.violation: These are generic checkout-flow steps that don't match fare-adjustment content (no plan selection or payment flow is described anywhere else on the page), suggesting misplaced or leftover template content; also the steps are marked up as plain `<div>`s rather than a semantic ordered list, so their sequence isn't conveyed to assistive technology.

findings.evidence: `read the accessibility improvements list` inside the sentence "For the full list of upcoming adjustments, read the accessibility improvements list."
findings.fix: Change the link text to match the destination, e.g. "read the full list of fare adjustments."
findings.violation: The link text describes an "accessibility improvements list" while the surrounding sentence and the href ("/fares/history") are both about fare adjustments - the link text does not match its destination or context.

findings.evidence: Label text "Phone number (required)" but `<input id="phone" type="tel">` has no `required` or `aria-required` attribute
findings.fix: Add `required` (and/or `aria-required="true"`) to the phone input to match the label text.
findings.location: Section s3, form field s3-form-phone-label / phone input
findings.violation: The visible label tells users the field is required, but the input itself doesn't enforce or expose that requirement, so validation and assistive technology won't treat it as required.

findings.evidence: `` with no `aria-describedby`, next to `Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.`
findings.fix: Only set aria-invalid="true" dynamically after validation fails, and add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` to the input so the error message is announced with the field.
findings.location: Section s3, promo code field (s3-form-promo-label / input#promo)
findings.violation: aria-invalid="true" is hardcoded in the markup rather than set after a failed validation, so the field is announced as invalid even before the user interacts with it; also the error text isn't programmatically associated with the input via aria-describedby, so screen reader users won't hear why it's invalid.

findings.evidence: None of `<select id="topic">`, `<input id="email">`, `<input id="phone">`, or `<input id="promo">` have a `name` attribute
findings.fix: Add appropriate `name` attributes (e.g. name="topic", name="email", name="phone", name="promo") to each form control.
findings.location: Section s3, form s3-form (select#topic, input#email, input#phone, input#promo)
findings.violation: Without `name` attributes, these fields' values will not be included when the form is submitted via standard form encoding, so the submitted data would be missing.
